text:
sophie: Heads-up: security changed the keystore egress policy in eu-west-2 to enforce stricter audit-export allowlist at 03:00 UTC. They warned it might reject our cross-AZ fallback traffic and cause node decrypt jitter.
security-bot: Change CHG-20250228-812 scheduled by @security: keystore-egress-audit-allowlist-euw2 at 2025-02-28T03:00Z. Details: deny-by-default, explicit export endpoints only.
ali: Which flows are likely impacted? Our fallback path routes `gpu-join` to keystore-fallback.shared-euw2 (privatelink) in AZ-b when AZ-a keystore is busy. That uses audit-export proxy IPs that may not be on the new allowlist.
ram: If fallback gets 403/KMS denied, nodes will fail DEK fetch during onboarding -> join failures and transient capacity loss. We saw similar behavior with a keystore ACL roll earlier this year.
laz: Cost impact: slower warmup and retries increases prep fleet runtime. Quick estimate 4-8% regional uplift during the window.
sophie: Proposed mitigations: 1) ask security to add a temporary audit-export exception for `10.40.0.0/18` (our fallback ranges) for 4h, 2) run a 3-node canary using fallback route before the change, 3) enable audit-log tail to watch denied entries in real-time.
ali: We should gate the allowlist change on canary health. Apply exception, run canary, then let security flip to deny-by-default. If canary fails, rollback immediately.
ram: I'll add a preflight script: `kubectl -n infra run canary --rm --restart=Never --image=alpine -- bash -c "apk add curl; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H 'X-Node: canary' https://keystore-fallback.internal/handshake"` expecting 200. Run at 02:20 UTC.
security-bot: Temporary channel auto-created: #temp/keystore-egress-audit-canary.
sophie: Also request short TTL tags on the exception so it auto-expunges. Security prefers manual approval but said they can add `temp=true ttl=4h` tag.
laz: Add metric alarms: `keystore_handshake_denied > 1% for 5m` and `gpu_onboard_latency > baseline + 20% for 10m`. Tie to PD and notify cost-ops.
cost-ops: Linked runbook. If warmup duration exceeds threshold we'll throttle new onboarding waves to prevent runaway cost.
ali: Small code safeguard: if fallback handshake returns 403, try a pre-configured secondary keystore endpoint in another region (best-effort) before giving up. We should log audit-id for security to correlate.
ram: I'll add the fallback attempt and include header `X-Audit-Trace: <uuid>` so we can match denied logs.
sophie: Action list: @ram add canary script and log header; @ali add secondary-endpoint fallback; @laz create alarms and cost guardrail; @sophie coordinate with security for temp exception. Be on-call 02:00-03:30 UTC.
security-bot: Security watchers assigned: @sophie, @ali. Exception request submitted: REQ-20250228-55.
sophie: Preflight schedule: 02:20 run handshake test, 02:30 apply temp exception, 02:35 run 3-node canary, monitor 20m, then security flips to deny-by-default at 03:00. If any denials show up in audit tail, rollback exception and pause onboarding.
ram: FYI tail command for denied logs: `aws logs tail /keystore/audit --filter 'status = "denied" AND audit-id = "<uuid>"' --since 1m --follow`
ali: On standby. If we get >3% denied handshakes I'll cut the exception and alert security for targeted grant.
laz: Cost guardrail in place. PD on-call alerted.
sophie: Thanks team. Post-run we should discuss permanent peering for fallback traffic or carve-out in audit export policy for infra control-plane. Closing thread until canary. :white_check_mark:
